notes: Particle (right) hand, entering from the lower right; posed independently of the left hand (not a transformed copy, review B1). Digit names follow user decision D1 (documentations/log/log-v2.md): INDEX = reaches up-left to the contact point; MIDDLE = the long digit pointing left beneath the index; THUMB = the short digit whose nail outline faces the viewer; RING and PINKY = the two digits curled down. CALIBRATED in log-v2 step 2 (2026-09-21/22) and RECALIBRATED on the step-3 builder (2026-09-24) against assets-source/reference/right-mask.png with scripts/compare_silhouette.py: every in-frame px and r (projected half-width in reference px) fitted to the reference silhouette, r tapering (non-increasing) from base to tip along every chain. DEPTH RECONSTRUCTED from the particle image, not copied from the left pose: with D1's digit order (index on top, thumb nail toward the viewer, thumb crossing in front of the palm) a right hand must turn its palm down and toward the camera, so the back of the hand faces up and AWAY from the camera (dorsal z < 0; D12 reads the top outline as the back of the index finger and the knuckles); the radial side (index, thumb) is nearest and the knuckles recede toward the little finger; flexing toward the palm therefore moves a digit down and toward the camera, which is why the ring and little fingers curl downward in the image; the thumb lies in front of the palm and of the curled ring and little fingers, whose middle phalanges pass behind it. The index sets the scale (2.3 px/mm) and its tip lies at the left index tip's depth (0.13), so the fingertips nearly touch in 3D. Every interphalangeal joint is a hinge: the depths of each finger's PIP, DIP and tip are solved so that its PIP and DIP bends lie in that finger's MCP flexion plane (the builder's transported dorsal frame; sideways parts <= 4 deg), with 3D phalanx lengths index 44:25:20, middle 45:27:27, ring 43:27:21, little 32:18:20 mm; the thumb is straight in projection, its IP a pure flexion (13.5 deg) and its MCP within 7 deg of its flexion plane, bones 49:28:27 mm. Thumb CMC set back in depth to 0.17 (D22: shortens the thenar fold); the thumbnail's fold (nail_start 0.22) lands on the drawn D's straight side at x ~950. Palm masses from step 3 (hypothenar, first dorsal interosseous, thenar) fill the drawn palm; the metacarpal plate is thinned (meta_base_thick 0.70, palm flat 0.17, hypothenar moved from palmar to ulnar) to a 31-36 mm mid-palm (was 36-43). dorsal is fitted perpendicular to the knuckle line and the wrist-to-knuckle axis. forearm lies outside the frame so the arm leaves it; the particle tail past the wrist is not modelled. Known limits: the palm stays thicker than an anatomical ~30 mm near the wrist (up to ~39 mm on its ulnar side at 0.3 of the way to the knuckles), because the reference palm band is taller in projection than a palm turned this far from the camera would be and thinning it further drops its top edge off the drawing; the MCP knuckles lie on a nearly straight line (middle ~2.6 mm palmar of the index-ring line), because moving them onto a convex arch pushes the middle/ring roots out of the drawn silhouette and packs ring and little finger into each other.
